title: Minimum Conference Rooms Provisioning
real_world_story: Corporate real estate planners are designing a new technology campus. They have analyzed the booking patterns of N scheduled daily meetings. Each meeting i occupies a conference room during the time interval [s_i, e_i). If meeting A ends at minute T and meeting B starts at minute T, both meetings can utilize the same conference room. To avoid renting excess office floors while guaranteeing zero booking conflicts, planners need to calculate the minimum number of physical conference rooms required.
problem_statement: Given N meeting intervals [s_i, e_i), find the minimum number of conference rooms required so that all meetings can take place without room overlap.
task: Determine the minimum number of conference rooms needed.
input_format:
The first line contains a single integer N, the number of meetings.
The next N lines each contain two space-separated integers s_i and e_i.
output_format: Print a single integer representing the minimum number of conference rooms required.

examples.explanation: Meeting 1 (0 to 30) runs continuously. Meeting 2 (5 to 10) and Meeting 3 (15 to 20) do not overlap each other and can share a second room. At most 2 meetings run concurrently at any time. Minimum rooms required = 2.
Meetings are contiguous without overlapping interior times: Room 1 can host [1, 5), then [5, 10), then [10, 15). Only 1 room is needed.

real_world_takeaway: Using a greedy sweep-line or min-heap to track active interval concurrency enables enterprise facility teams to right-size physical office infrastructure.
